analysis.title: FX Daily: Uneasy calm as markets stabilise
key_insights: After a week of tech-led selling the S&P 500 fell nearly 9% on the week and is over 12% below last month's high. Equity futures are marked 2% higher today.
The IT sector fell 7% on Friday with a 34% S&P 500 weight and did most of the damage. Defensive sectors like consumer staples posted net gains, so there was no full capitulation.
ING says the dollar can hold its gains because a hawkish Fed undercurrent persists. October core PCE due Wednesday looks set to come in hot and support a tightening cycle into 2027.
Treasury Secretary Bessent said many people believe the Fed may be making a policy mistake if it overtightens. A less aggressive Fed would help stabilise equities.
A reversal in copper or precious metals could signal dollar buying pressure has peaked. Until then ING expects USD, JPY and CHF defensive currencies to stay in demand.
ING does not see DXY correcting much below the 103.35/50 area today, with US S&P PMI expected on the strong side.

EUR/USD held narrow ranges last week despite the tech selloff, even as nearly 30bp was priced out of the 2027 Fed tightening cycle. ING attributes this to long dollar positioning and option strike congestion at 1.0850/0950.
EUR/USD correction is not seen going much beyond 1.1030 short term. A close above 1.11 this week would relieve a weak EUR/USD story as seasonal dollar weakness approaches.

EU leaders are due to decide on the next ECB President on Thursday. Polymarket gives Pablo Hernandez de Cos a 96% chance, and ING expects the Chief Economist role to go to a northern European as a counterweight.

SNB Vice President Martin warned inflation is picking up (October CPI 1.5% y/y). Markets price unchanged policy into year-end but two hikes by next September. ING sees downside risks for EUR/CHF with a possible retest of 0.9125.
CEE currencies all tested new local lows on Friday under global pressure and dovish regional central banks. ING remains bearish despite possible near-term relief.
In the Czech Republic Moody's upgraded its outlook to stable and S&P reviews on Friday, with a similar move possible. CNB officials called the recent hike pre-emptive against energy price spillover.

sector_views.rationale: Tech-led selling drove the S&P 500 drop, with IT down 7% on Friday. ING offers no formal rating, only the observation.
Defensive sectors such as staples posted net gains on Friday.

ING sees no need for DXY to correct much below this area.

CEE currencies exposed to global pressure and dovish regional central banks.

Money markets price two SNB hikes by next September and unchanged policy into year-end.
geopolitical: Energy price spillover into broader inflation is cited by CNB officials as the reason for the recent Czech hike.
